result.markdown: --- title: "Sensitivity and identifiability" course-unit: ch10-sensitivity-and-identifiability status: complete --- ## Why this unit matters - **Sensitivity:** which inputs move a chosen output? - **Identifiability:** which parameters can the observation process distinguish? - A narrow optimizer interval is not evidence that every biological parameter is learned. ::: {.notes} This deck is a map of the detailed book chapter. Keep the distinction between perturbing a model and learning from data visible throughout the presentation. ::: ## Baseline SIR model Deterministic, continuous-time, continuous-state, population model: $$ \dot S=-\beta cSI/N,\qquad \dot I=\beta cSI/N-\gamma I,\qquad \dot R=\gamma I. $$ At the course baseline, $N=1000$, $(S,I,R)=(990,10,0)$, $(\beta,c,\gamma)=(0.05,10,0.25)$, and $\mathcal R_0=\beta c/\gamma=2$. The state sensitivity matrix is $J_x(t)=\partial x(t)/\partial(\beta,c,\gamma)$. ::: {.notes} The product beta times c is the transmission rate in this model. That observation previews the structural identifiability result. ::: ## Local sensitivity: a derivative, not an uncertainty interval For a small perturbation, $$ \Delta z\approx\nabla_\theta z\,\Delta\theta. $$ The following small solve uses `OrdinaryDiffEq` and centered perturbations to plot the infectious-state derivative at the baseline. ::: {#cell-fig-slide-ch10-local .cell execution_count=1} ::: {#fig-slide-ch10-local .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html} ``` Centered local derivatives of infectious prevalence. ::: ::: ::: {.notes} The derivative is local to the baseline and depends on the chosen output, time, and parameterization. A derivative is not a posterior distribution. ::: ## Global variation and the observation map Global analysis varies a plausible parameter box and summarizes an output such as peak infectious prevalence. `GlobalSensitivity.gsa` can replace the small grid below with a Sobol design; the interpretation still depends on the bounds. ::: {#cell-fig-slide-ch10-global .cell execution_count=1} ::: {#fig-slide-ch10-global .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html} ``` One-at-a-time output ranges over a plausible parameter box. ::: ::: Only incidence is observed: $$ y(t)=\beta c\,S(t)I(t)/N. $$ The transformation $(\beta,c)\mapsto(a\beta,c/a)$ leaves this map unchanged. Thus $\beta$ and $c$ are structurally confounded; $\beta c$ can be learned. ::: {.notes} StructuralIdentifiability.jl formalizes this result with differential algebra. More data do not automatically help if they repeat the same observation map; contact-pattern data or an externally measured c would. ::: ## API and validation ```julia local_problem = ODEForwardSensitivityProblem(sir_kernel!, u0, (0.0, 40.0), p0) local_solution = solve(local_problem, Tsit5(); saveat = tgrid) states, jacobians = extract_local_sensitivities(local_solution, true) identifiability = assess_identifiability( identifiability_system; measured_quantities = [y ~ b * c * S * I], funcs_to_check = [b, c, g, b * c], ) ``` - `SciMLSensitivity`: forward sensitivities or adjoints. - `GlobalSensitivity`: Sobol first-order and total indices. - `StructuralIdentifiability`: structural, noiseless identifiability. - Check $S+I+R=N$ and compare one derivative with a finite difference. ::: {.notes} The API snippet points to the full implementation in the book. The validation checks numerical integrity, not historical adequacy or causal interpretation. ::: ## Takeaways and limitations - Local: neighborhood behavior around one parameter vector. - Global: ranking conditional on ranges and a design. - Structural: information available in an idealized observation map. - Practical identifiability also depends on noise, sampling, initial states, and misspecification. Read the [book chapter](../../chapters/10-sensitivity-and-identifiability.html) for derivations and exercises; see the [SciMLSensitivity](https://docs.sciml.ai/SciMLSensitivity/stable/), [GlobalSensitivity](https://docs.sciml.ai/GlobalSensitivity/stable/), and [StructuralIdentifiability](https://docs.sciml.ai/StructuralIdentifiability/stable/) documentation for APIs. ::: {.notes} Close by asking which conclusion is about the model and which is about the data. That question is the bridge to intervention analysis and the capstone. :::
